heading: What our users say
intro: From finding the right words to getting started. Experiences, small wins, and ideas for what comes next.
note: Translated from user submissions. Experiences and plans may differ by edition; see current Global plans for pricing and features.

entries.quote: After using it a few times, I've found the responses pretty quick. Ideas usually appear shortly after the interviewer finishes asking, so I don't end up sitting through long silences during the interview.
I've tried a few other interview assistants, and they were quite expensive. This one's pricing feels more manageable for someone like me who only needs it while looking for a job.
My favorite part is being able to upload my resume and the job description beforehand. The answers aren't just generic AI responses; they draw on my project experience. That's genuinely useful.
I was a little worried it would be complicated at first, but after starting a session I pretty much understood how to use it. I'd still like to see a more detailed guide for new users.
I'm interviewing for technical roles. For questions about projects and some technical topics, the suggested approach is useful. At the very least, it helps me organize what I want to say quickly.
Screenshot answers are convenient, especially when the interviewer suddenly sends a question or shares one on screen. I don't have to type the whole thing out myself.
I bought a one-day plan just to try it, then renewed when I had more interviews. I'd love an option to buy access by the number of sessions in the future.
It's really helpful when you get nervous around people 😂 Sometimes I know the answer, but my mind goes blank in an interview. Having a prompt beside me makes me feel a lot more at ease.
Responses are faster than with some tools I've tried, and the transcription is fairly good. A sentence is occasionally transcribed inaccurately, though. I hope that keeps improving.
For me, the biggest benefit isn't having it answer for you. It's getting a framework for an answer. Once I have a direction, I can put it into my own words and sound much more natural.
Importing my resume makes a noticeable difference compared with asking AI directly. When the interviewer follows up on past projects, it can give me prompts based on what's in my resume.
The interface is clean, without a clutter of features. A complicated interface is the last thing I want during an interview, so keeping it simple works better for me.
I'm a new graduate and used it for my first formal interview. I don't know the result yet, but the process felt much smoother than my previous interviews on my own.
I'd like more role-specific modes, such as product management, operations, algorithms, Java, and frontend development, with the answer style adapting automatically to the role.
Price was one of the main reasons I chose it. I looked at a range of similar products, and some monthly prices really are quite high for students.
Being able to recognize both computer audio and the microphone is important. The interviewer's questions are transcribed automatically, so I don't have to copy and paste them myself.
An interviewer once asked several follow-up questions in a row. The AI could still use the earlier context rather than treating each question as completely separate. That was a good experience.
I'd suggest a post-interview review that automatically brings together the questions, my answers, and areas to improve. I think that would be really useful.

At first I thought a tool like this would noticeably disrupt the interview. In practice, treating it as a prompt rather than reading it word for word doesn't really get in the way of a normal conversation.

Overall, it's a practical interview assistant at a price I can accept. My main hope now is for continued improvements to speech recognition accuracy and response time. Better stability would make it even better.
